cohort: Women who gave birth to a singleton, liveborn neonate
finding: Pregnancies complicated by fetal CHD had a significantly higher rate of operative vaginal delivery, primarily due to non-reassuring fetal heart rate, compared to pregnancies without CHD.
mod_finding: Operative vaginal delivery, performed mostly because of non-reassuring fetal heart rate, is more common in pregnancies complicated by a prenatal diagnosis of CHD than non-anomalous pregnancies.
